Your product pages,

rewritten to convert.
Home.lead: AI audit in about a minute. Per-product score. Titles, descriptions and photos rewritten — you stay in control.
Home.urlHint: Public storefront URL. We auto-detect the platform.
Home.howItWorksTitle: From URL to AI-generated upgrades in three steps.
Home.step1Description: Drop your store URL — or set up your store yourself if it isn't online yet. We auto-detect Shopify / WooCommerce / Wix and score every product across catalog, copy, visual quality and tagging in about a minute.
Home.step2Title: Pick the model, set the tone
Home.step2Description: Choose your text model — Gemini 3.1 Pro by Google, or Claude Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.6 by Anthropic — and your image quality (1K, 2K or 4K) on GPT-Image 2 by OpenAI. Add brand-voice instructions if you want, applied site-wide or per product.
Home.step3Description: Get a fresh title, description and tags, plus 3 lifestyle photo angles. Copy the text, download the images, and ship them on your store.
Home.seoTitle: OneShopLab — AI product page optimization for Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix
Home.seoDescription: Audit your storefront in about a minute. Score every product on copy, visuals, catalog and tags. AI rewrites, regenerates and redesigns — with prompts you control.

Pricing.title: Plans for every catalog size
Pricing.subtitle: Pick a monthly subscription with fresh credits each renewal — or top up with credit packs that never expire. Every plan unlocks every model. Cancel anytime.
Pricing.whatIsCreditBody: A credit is the unit you spend on every AI generation. Costs depend on the model and image quality you pick — heavier models and higher resolutions consume more. Here are typical costs at the default Sonnet 4.6 + 1k settings:
Pricing.faq1A: Subscription credits reset every month. Free signup credits stay on your account until used.
Pricing.faq2Q: Can I switch models per generation?
Pricing.faq2A: Yes — set your default in Preferences, and every generation uses your account-wide setting. You can change it anytime to apply to future runs.
Pricing.faq3Q: What happens when I run out of credits?
Pricing.faq3A: Generations stop until you upgrade or your monthly cycle renews. Failed generations are refunded automatically.
Pricing.faq4A: Anytime, no questions asked. Your account stays active till the end of the current billing period.

overall.poor: The overall score signals a catalog with significant gaps. Closing them — starting with the weakest axis — drives the biggest absolute lift in traffic and conversion.
overall.mid: A solid baseline is in place. A focused pass on the weaker axes — usually description length, alt text and tagging — pushes past 75 and unlocks more SEO and conversion.
overall.good: A strong catalog overall, which directly supports SEO ranking, conversion and shopper trust. Remaining gains come from polishing the long tail of products.

catalog.poor: Catalog completeness at {value}/100 — too many products are missing core fields like images, descriptions or tags; filling these in unlocks indexing, ranking and basic shopper trust.
catalog.mid: Catalog completeness at {value}/100 — most products are complete but a meaningful share still has gaps; closing them improves indexability and reduces bounce.
catalog.good: Catalog completeness at {value}/100 — products have the essentials in place, strengthening search-engine indexability and giving shoppers everything they need at a glance.

copy.poor: Copy quality at {value}/100 — descriptions are short, unstructured or missing on many products; improving them increases organic search visibility and gives shoppers reasons to buy.
copy.mid: Copy quality at {value}/100 — descriptions exist but vary widely in length and structure; deeper, scannable copy boosts both SEO and conversion.
copy.good: Copy quality at {value}/100 — descriptions are substantial and well-structured, which directly helps SEO ranking and gives buyers the confidence to convert.

visual.poor: Visual quality at {value}/100 — too few images, missing alt text or low-resolution shots hurt SEO and trust; richer visuals lift conversion noticeably.
visual.mid: Visual quality at {value}/100 — most products have at least one decent image but coverage is uneven; consistent quality visuals reduce returns and push add-to-cart up.
visual.good: Visual quality at {value}/100 — products have multiple high-resolution images with alt text, boosting image-search visibility and shopper confidence.

tagging.poor: Tagging at {value}/100 — products carry few or no discovery tags, hurting on-site search and SEO; adding tags is one of the cheapest wins.
tagging.mid: Tagging at {value}/100 — basic tags are in place but discovery could be richer; better tagging improves on-site search relevance.
tagging.good: Tagging at {value}/100 — strong tag coverage powers on-site search, faceted navigation and SEO, helping more shoppers land on the right product faster.

avgScore.poor: Average product score is {value}/100 — most products would benefit from a thorough pass on copy, images and tags.
avgScore.mid: Average product score is {value}/100 — there's a clear tail of weaker products dragging the catalog down; lifting them lifts the whole.
avgScore.good: Average product score is {value}/100 — overall product quality is solid, translating into stronger conversion across the catalog.

avgImages.poor: {value} images per product on average — well below the 3+ baseline; adding 2-3 lifestyle shots typically lifts add-to-cart by double digits.
avgImages.mid: {value} images per product on average — close to the 3+ baseline; pushing to 4-5 with lifestyle shots reduces returns and increases trust.
avgImages.good: {value} images per product on average — meets the 3+ baseline, giving shoppers enough visual angles to commit with confidence.

avgDescLength.poor: Descriptions average {value} characters — too short to cover benefits, specs and use cases, which limits both SEO and conversion.
avgDescLength.mid: Descriptions average {value} characters — workable but room for more depth; richer copy drives SEO and reduces pre-purchase questions.
avgDescLength.good: Descriptions average {value} characters — substantial enough to convince and rank, doing the heavy lifting on SEO and conversion.

avgTags.poor: {value} tags per product on average — discovery and faceted browsing will suffer; even 5 well-chosen tags unlocks meaningful traffic.
avgTags.mid: {value} tags per product on average — adequate but could be richer; targeted long-tail tags compound on top of basic SEO.
avgTags.good: {value} tags per product on average — strong coverage feeds on-site search, faceted navigation and long-tail SEO.

productsNoImage.none: Every product has at least one image — no blind spots in the catalog.
productsNoImage.some: {count} product(s) have no image at all — these are conversion dead zones, fix them in priority.

productsNoDesc.none: Every product has a description — full copy coverage.
productsNoDesc.some: {count} product(s) have no description — silently kill SEO and conversion, even a short paragraph helps.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before you start.
Faq.ctaBody: Run a free audit on your store. No card, no commitment — see the score, sample the AI, decide for yourself.
Faq.ctaSignupHint: Or skip straight to your 150 free credits
Faq.q01a: Yes. Every new account gets 150 free credits, no card required. Enough to audit one store and run a full AI generation (title + description + tags + 3 images) on roughly one to two products — enough to judge the output quality before you spend anything.
Faq.q02q: Will the AI sound generic or robotic?
Faq.q02a: You control the tone. Add a brand-voice instruction once site-wide (or per product) — "warm, casual, no exclamation marks" — and OneShopLab passes it to the model you pick: Gemini 3.1 Pro by Google, or Claude Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.6 by Anthropic. The output is generated against your actual product attributes, not a template.
Faq.q03a: Shopify, WooCommerce and Wix natively — we auto-detect the platform from your store URL. No existing store? You can also set up your own store inside OneShopLab: create a project, add products manually (title, description, images), then use the same AI rewriter and audit on top.
Faq.q04q: Do I have to install anything on my store?
Faq.q04a: No app, no permissions to grant. Generations happen on OneShopLab. You copy the new title and description, download the images, and paste them into your store admin when you're happy.
Faq.q05q: Are my original product texts and images preserved?
Faq.q05a: Always. AI outputs live on OneShopLab as a side-by-side before/after history. Nothing is pushed to your store unless you put it there yourself.
Faq.q06q: What happens if I run out of credits?
Faq.q06a: Your audits, history and content stay accessible. Top-up packs are available on the Pricing page (one-off, no auto-renew), or you can upgrade to a higher plan for a larger monthly allowance.
Faq.q07q: Can I cancel my subscription anytime?
Faq.q07a: Yes. From Account → Subscription, open the Stripe billing portal and cancel in a click. You keep access until the end of the current billing period, and any unused credits stay spendable on your account.
Faq.q08q: Why use OneShopLab instead of ChatGPT directly?
Faq.q08a: ChatGPT gives you the model. OneShopLab gives you the workflow: automatic audit of your whole catalog, per-product scoring, versioned before/after history, one-click "Generate all" per product (every plan), and bulk generation across thousands of products on Pro and Scale. Same models, ten times less manual work.
Faq.q09q: In which languages can I generate content?
Faq.q09a: The interface ships in 13 languages, and you can set the output language per site — useful for multi-locale stores where the French site needs French copy and the German site needs German.
Faq.q10q: Is my data safe? Do you train models on it?
Faq.q10a: Our database and web app run on OVH in France (EU); images are stored on Cloudflare R2. Prompts are routed through kie.ai to Anthropic / Google / OpenAI under no-training agreements (providers may retain prompts up to 30 days for abuse prevention only). Full sub-processor list on our Privacy page.
Faq.q11q: Do I need to know prompt engineering?
Faq.q11a: No. Default prompts are tuned per model and per field (title, description, tags, images). The optional brand-voice field is plain instructions — written the way you'd brief a copywriter.
Faq.q12a: A typical store of around 50 products audits in about 1 to 1.5 minutes. Larger catalogs scale linearly — we fetch up to 10,000 products per audit — and per-product scores stream in as soon as each product is processed.
